tools.name: run
tools.description:
Runs JavaScript against the user's browser and returns what the script returns. `code` is the body of an async function: `await` each SDK call and `return` a JSON value. Each run starts with fresh JavaScript. With no task, built-in `page` opens a new tab on first use; `context.newPage()` opens another. Neither reuses a tab or creates a task.

To keep tabs across runs, create a task and return its id. First run: `const task = await neo.createTask('hn top 5'); return task.id`. Start later scripts with `await neo.task('<id>')`; then `page` uses the task's last-used open tab (else another open tab, else a new one), and `context.newPage()` opens in the task. The latest task pick wins. Use `task.pages()` (oldest first), `task.page(tabId)` or `task.newPage()` as needed. When finished: `await task.close()`. Popups join their opener's task. `context.pages()` lists every tab with `page.tabId` and `page.taskId` (null without a task); use it to recover a lost task id.

The function's parameters are the SDK: Playwright's `page`, `context`, `browser`, `expect` and `playwright` (`selectors.setTestIdAttribute`, `errors.TimeoutError`), Node's `Buffer` (`screenshot` and `pdf` resolve to one, and a `setInputFiles` payload takes one), then `neo` (the `neo.*` methods listed below), `console` (its lines come back with the result), `setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, `NeoError` and `TimeoutError`. The realm is QuickJS, which has no `Intl`.

`timeout` is in milliseconds: 300000 by default, at most 900000. The returned value is at most 256 KiB of JSON; bytes in it (a `Buffer`, such as a `screenshot` or `pdf`) that would take it over come back as `{"$neo":"blob","id","size"}`, which the host reads, so return large text as `Buffer.from(text)`.

An SDK call that fails throws a `NeoError` with `code`, `owner` (who must fix it: neo, script, website or host), `delivery`, `retryable` and `operationId`; a timeout throws its subclass `TimeoutError`. `delivery: "unknown"` means a write may have happened: look at the page before repeating it. `retryable: true` means a repeat is safe (nothing was sent, or the call only read); it is never a promise that a repeat will succeed, so read the `message` before trying again.

`page.ariaSnapshot()` lists what you can act on, with refs; `page.getByRef('e5')` acts on one; `{ text: true }` adds the page's text. An element without a ref is reached with a locator (`page.getByText('…')`). A field printed without a ref has no size or takes no pointer: reach it by role and name, `page.getByRole('textbox', { name: '…' })`; `pressSequentially('…')` types into it and fails if it cannot take the focus; `fill` works only if it has a size. `page.getByRef('e12').ariaSnapshot({ mode: 'full' })` prints all of one section as Playwright does, with its text and a ref on each visible element, up to `maxTokens`; a whole page that way is several times larger.

SDK methods:

- Playwright's API on `page`, `context` and `browser`, as Playwright 1.64.1 behaves where this does not say otherwise: locators (`getByRole`, `getByText`, `getByLabel`, `getByTestId`, `locator`, `frameLocator`, `filter`, `nth`) that wait and are strict, frames (`page.frames()`, `frame.locator`), reads (`textContent`, `innerText`, `getAttribute`, `inputValue`, `count`, `isVisible`, `page.content()`, `page.title()`), actions that wait until the element is actionable (`click`, `dblclick`, `hover`, `fill`, `clear`, `press`, `pressSequentially`, `check`, `uncheck`, `setChecked`, `selectOption`, `selectText`, `focus`, `blur`, `dragTo`, `drop`, `dispatchEvent`, `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded`; no `tap`), `page.keyboard` (`press`, `type`, `insertText`, `down`, `up`), `page.mouse` (`move`, `down`, `up`, `click`, `dblclick`, `wheel`), navigation (`goto`, `reload`, `goBack`, `goForward`, `waitForURL`, `waitForLoadState`, `waitForNavigation`), scripts in the page's main world (`page.evaluate`, `page.waitForFunction`, `locator.evaluate`, `locator.evaluateAll`, `locator.waitForFunction`, `elementHandle.evaluate`, and `$eval` (`evalOnSelector`) and `$$eval` on a page, frame or element handle; a `frame` form runs in its frame, a child frame too) with Playwright's values, arguments, element handles and errors, `page.requestGC` (its main renderer's garbage collection), `page.emulateMedia` (per page across runs and navigations), `page.setViewportSize` (the tab keeps the size in later runs, until it closes), `page.addScriptTag` and `page.addStyleTag` (also on frames), returning element handles, `page.setContent` and `frame.setContent`, whose HTML's scripts run there too, init scripts (`page.addInitScript`, `context.addInitScript`) that every new document runs in its main world, bindings the page calls back into the script with (`exposeBinding`, `exposeFunction`, on a page or the context, and the `exposeFunctions` option of `addInitScript` and of `evaluate`; the prelude answers each call with `bindingCall.resolve`), `screenshot` and `pdf`, events (`page.on`, `waitForEvent`), downloads (`download.path()` waits for the file and returns where the browser saved it, which a later run can upload with `setInputFiles`; `saveAs(path)` copies it; `failure()`), and `expect`: retrying locator matchers (`toBeVisible`, `toBeChecked`, `toHaveText`, `toContainText`, `toHaveValue`, `toHaveCount`, `toHaveAttribute`, ...), page matchers (`toHaveTitle`, `toHaveURL`) and `toMatchAriaSnapshot` on either with the template as a YAML string, with `.not`, value matchers (`toBe`, `toEqual`, ...), `expect.poll` and `toPass`; soft assertions, `toBeOK`, screenshot comparisons and snapshot files are not available. In hosted BrowserOS, by design, a script receives no console messages, no page errors and no browser log entries: console and pageerror listeners are accepted but stay silent, and `page.waitForEvent` for either fails immediately with `neo/unsupported`; exposed bindings work. A call that waits gives up after 5 s unless given a `timeout`, and a navigation after 30 s. Unlike Playwright, `waitForFunction` polls every 100 ms for its default `polling: 'raf'`, since animation frames never fire in Neo's background tabs, and the handle it resolves to holds a snapshot of the value, which `jsonValue()` reads; `setContent` refuses `waitUntil: 'networkidle'`, which Neo cannot observe after a write, with nothing sent; and a result nested more than about 50 objects deep can fail `Maximum call stack size exceeded`, where Playwright allows 98. `goto` opens `http`, `https`, `data`, `about` and `javascript` URLs; Chromium executes a `javascript:` URL before reporting `net::ERR_ABORTED`. `reload` opens only `http`, `https`, `data` and `about` URLs. A script cannot open `file:` pages: `goto` refuses a `file:` URL, `goBack` and `goForward` a `file:` history entry, and every call on a tab that shows a `file:` page (one the owner opened) is refused, with nothing sent; a call whose tab moves onto one while it runs gets no answer from it. Write a local page with `page.setContent` instead. Path reads (`setInputFiles`, `drop`, script/style tags and init scripts) must be inside the host's `files.readDirs`, the downloads folder by default. Neo's own files are always protected from reads and writes. Use `download.path()` for downloaded files or ask the host to allow a staging folder. A relative path uses Neo's working directory. `{ name, mimeType, buffer }` payloads need no allowed folder and total under 10 MiB a call. A directory upload needs its tab in front, and the tabs Neo opens for an agent stay in the background (`bringToFront` is refused). An init script or a binding stays registered until the run ends, then its tab no longer has it; a context's reaches each tab before the run's first write to it, so a popup's first document and cross-site iframes run without it. A page's call of a binding reaches the script through the event pump, so a call the page does not await (from an event handler) may run after the op that caused it returned. A function `evaluate` passes stays exposed until the run ends; `evaluateHandle` has no `exposeFunctions`.

- neo.createTask(name?) -> Task: start a task, your own set of tabs; return task.id and keep it

- neo.task(id) -> Task: a task from an earlier run (task.id, task.pages(), task.page(tabId), task.newPage(), task.close())

inputSchema.description:
The `run` tool's arguments, and, derived from this type, its input schema: what a model
sends and what it reads about it are one definition. Unknown fields and `timeout: null` are
refused rather than ignored: the model meant something by them. The field docs are the
schema's descriptions.

code.description:
JavaScript: the body of an async function. `await` each SDK call and `return` a JSON
value.

session.description: Opaque logical task handle. When a client has no transport session, the server returns it in every result. Pass it as session on later calls to keep the same SDK task. Find its pages with context.pages() and page.taskId. Omit it on the first call or to start a separate task after Stop; a stopped handle stays stopped.

timeout.description: The run's budget in milliseconds, from 1 to 900000. Leave it out for 300000.

inputSchema.title: RunArgs

tools.name: request_human_help
tools.description: Ask a human to take over a tab for sign-in, a one-time code, a captcha, an account choice, or an approval. Pass page.tabId from a run script as page, a short reason, and optionally details, resumeHint and kind. This waits briefly and returns the same tab id as page. If status is waiting, call await_human_help until resolved, cancelled or timed_out. Do nothing else on that tab while waiting.

details.description: What the human should know to help, e.g. where the code was sent.

kind.description: The kind of help, used for the cockpit icon.

page.description: The native tab id from page.tabId in a run script. The cockpit brings exactly this tab to the front.

reason.description: A short line saying what you need a human to do, e.g. "Enter the LinkedIn verification code".

resumeHint.description: What you will do after, so the human knows the task continues, e.g. "I'll pick up at profile 15 of 22".

session.description: Opaque logical task handle. When a client has no transport session, the server returns it in every result. Pass it as session on later calls to keep the same SDK task. Find its pages with context.pages() and page.taskId. Omit it on the first call or to start a separate task after Stop; a stopped handle stays stopped.

tools.name: await_human_help
tools.description: Keep waiting on an open human-help request. Call this repeatedly after request_human_help until the status is "resolved" (the human handed control back), "cancelled" (the run was stopped), or "timed_out" (no human responded in time). Do nothing else on the page while waiting.

requestId.description: The requestId returned by request_human_help. Optional; the server correlates this request by session.
